value_stream.name: Employee Transport, Shuttle & Daily Commute Management

fields.Owner: Head of HR Shared Services / Transport Lead (VS-103)
fields.Participants: Store/DC Ops (VS-07/VS-04), Workforce Planning (VS-103.3), Finance (VS-17.4), Strategy (VS-33), Real Estate (VS-97)
fields.Trigger: Annual workforce/transport planning; new-store opening (VS-37); shift-pattern change
fields.Volume: Enterprise: ~6,762 employees across 205 sites; ~5,800 store staff on 2–3 shifts

Automation Opportunity: - Geocoded home-distribution mapping; shift-roster → transport-need auto-derivation; gap-heat-map dashboard
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: need-assessment evidence-based (geocoded); strategy approved (CHRO/COO); aligned to workforce plan (VS-103.3)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.3 (workforce planning), VS-19.3 (shifts), VS-28 (analytics), VS-37 (new-store trigger), VS-97/VS-07 (sites), W4244 (operating model), W4250 (routes)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coverage-blind risk**: Need unquantified → shuttle/allowance mis-sized (over-spend or stranded staff); mitigated by geocoded home-distribution + shift-mapped gap analysis
- **Equity risk**: Some sites/shifts favored; mitigated by transparent service-tier criteria
System Touchpoints: - Workforce planning/roster (VS-103.3 / VS-19.3 shift data); HRIS employee address & shift (VS-19); analytics (VS-28); store/DC locations (VS-97/VS-07); strategy (VS-33)
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks annual assessment; site add/change triggers a 1-week refresh

steps.activity: HR/Ops run an annual commute-need assessment per site: employee home-location distribution (geocoded), shift roster start/end times vs local public-transport availability, after-dark safety exposure, and ride-share/jeepney/tricycle feasibility
steps.r: Transport Lead / Workforce Planning / Site Mgrs

steps.activity: HR/Ops quantify the transport gap (employees per site needing assisted commute, by shift), size the service need (routes, seats, trips/shift), and prioritize sites (after-hours shifts, unsafe corridors, high-attrition stores)

HR/Strategy set the transport strategy (service tiers, owned vs contracted mix, allowance vs shuttle, ESG/rideshare goals), obtain approval, and cascade to operating-model (W4244) and route design (W4250)

fields.Owner: Head of HR Shared Services / HR Policy (VS-103.1)
fields.Participants: Labor Relations (VS-84), Legal (VS-100.3), Comp (VS-102), Contingent Workforce (VS-98)
fields.Volume: One enterprise transport policy governing ~6,762 employees

Automation Opportunity: - Policy-in-system eligibility rules (shift/role/site) driving auto-entitlement; ESS policy acknowledgement tracking
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: policy Legal/Comp-reviewed; tax treatment documented (W4243); CBA-consistent (VS-84); published & acknowledged
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.1 (policy/ESS), VS-84 (labor/CBA), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-102 (comp), VS-98 (contingent), W4243 (tax), W4251 (entitlement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-classification risk**: Allowance construed as taxable wage or CBA benefit; mitigated by Legal/Comp tax-treatment review (W4243) and CBA alignment (VS-84)
- **Co-employment risk**: Contingent staff transported without guardrail; mitigated by parity rules aligned to VS-98
System Touchpoints: - HR policy/ESS (VS-103.1); HRIS (VS-19); labor relations (VS-84); legal (VS-100.3); comp (VS-102); contingent workforce (VS-98)

steps.activity: HR Policy author the transport policy: who is eligible (shift, role, site, distance, contingent-worker parity per VS-98), service vs allowance rules, late/early-shift coverage windows, no-show/cancellation rules, and guest/visitor rules

HR Policy/Legal align the policy to DOLE Labor Code (not a wage/benefit guarantee unless CBA — coordinate VS-84), BIR tax treatment of transport allowance (de minimis / non-taxable limits), and contingent-worker co-employment guardrails (VS-98)
HR Policy publish the policy (employee handbook / ESS VS-103.1), train site managers on enforcement, and establish the exception/approval path

fields.Participants: HR Shared Services (VS-103), Payroll (VS-19.2), Legal/Tax (VS-100.3/VS-79), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Policy (W4242); annual comp cycle; fuel/price change
fields.Volume: Allowance rates per site-zone × shift-type, paid to eligible employees

workflows.name: Transport-Allowance Design, Rate Setting & Tax Treatment

Automation Opportunity: - Rate-table auto-application by zone×shift; payroll-vs-shuttle cost decision-support; tax-limit auto-flagging
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: rates Finance-justified; BIR tax treatment documented (VS-79); payroll-coded & tested (VS-19.2)
Cross-references: - links to VS-102 (comp), VS-19.2 (payroll), VS-79 (tax), VS-17.4 (finance), W4242 (eligibility), W4244 (model comparison)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tax-leak risk**: Mis-coded allowance → undisclosed taxable benefit / BIR exposure; mitigated by BIR-limit-aligned rates and Payroll coding
- **Cost-creep risk**: Allowance drifts above shuttle cost; mitigated by modeled shuttle-vs-allowance comparison (W4244) and annual review
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks annual design; payroll config ~1 week

steps.activity: Comp/Finance set allowance rates by site-zone (distance band), shift type, and mode, benchmarked to local transport cost (fuel, jeepney/tricycle fare, ride-share), and modeled vs the cost of operating a shuttle (W4244)
Tax/Legal determine BIR treatment (de minimis/non-taxable transport allowance limits under TRAIN, or taxable if exceeding), coordinate with VS-79 (EWT/compensation) and VS-19.2 payroll coding
Payroll/Comp configure the allowance in the payroll engine (rate table by zone×shift, eligibility from W4242), test, and launch; monitor cost and tax impact

fields.Volume: Operating-model decision per site-cluster (owned shuttle, leased, contracted charter, rideshare/vanpool, or allowance-only)

workflows.name: Transport Operating-Model Decision (Owned vs Leased vs Contracted vs Allowance)

Automation Opportunity: - TCO scenario modeling (owned/leased/contracted/allowance); supply-market cost benchmarking
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: model Finance-TCO-justified per cluster; liability/insurance structured (VS-26); approved (COO/CFO)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06/VS-35 (fleet/asset), VS-34 (procurement), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-26 (insurance), VS-100.3 (legal), W4243 (allowance), W4245 (fleet), W4257 (vendor)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Model-mismatch risk**: Owned fleet where vendor is cheaper (or vice versa); mitigated by per-cluster TCO
- **Liability risk**: Contracted/rideshare shifts liability unclearly; mitigated by Legal/insurance structuring (VS-26/VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Transport/Finance build the TCO comparison per option (owned fleet incl. driver/depreciation/maintenance/insurance per VS-06/VS-35; leased; contracted charter per-trip; rideshare/vanpool per-employee; vs pure allowance per W4243)
Procurement/Fleet assess supply market (qualified shuttle/charter vendors per region, LTFRB-franchised), and Legal assess liability/insurance structure for each model (VS-26, VS-100.3)
Transport/Leadership decide the model per cluster, obtain approval, and trigger fleet plan (W4245), vendor sourcing (W4257), or allowance rollout (W4243)

fields.Participants: Fleet (VS-06), Finance Capex (VS-40), Real Estate (VS-97), Insurance (VS-26)
fields.Volume: Shuttle vehicles sized to peak-shift seat demand across prioritized sites

workflows.name: Shuttle Fleet Requirement, Capital & Leasing Plan

Automation Opportunity: - Peak-shift demand → fleet-sizing models; utilization/capacity dashboards; registration/insurance expiry tracking
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: fleet demand-justified; capex approved (VS-40); registered (LTO) & insured (VS-26) before service
Cross-references: - links to VS-06.2 (fleet), VS-40/VS-35 (capex/asset), VS-61 (fleet TCO), VS-26 (insurance), VS-97/VS-138 (parking), VS-37 (new-store sequencing), W4260 (compliance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-/over-capacity risk**: Wrong seat count vs peak shift; mitigated by peak-shift demand sizing + utilization monitoring (W4264)
- **Compliance risk**: Unregistered/uninsured vehicles; mitigated by LTO registration + insurance gate before service (W4260)
System Touchpoints: - Fleet management (VS-06.2); fixed asset/capex (VS-40/VS-35); fleet TCO (VS-61); insurance (VS-26); real estate/parking (VS-97/VS-138)
Time Estimate: - ~3 weeks annual plan; per-vehicle onboarding ~1–2 weeks

steps.activity: Transport/Fleet size the shuttle fleet (peak-shift seats per route, vehicle type — coaster/van/minibus, utilization, spare ratio), and the parking/staging need at sites (coordinate VS-97/VS-138)
Finance/Fleet build the capex/lease business case (buy vs lease vs finance), route through capex approval (VS-40), and align to fleet TCO (VS-61) and insurance (VS-26)
Fleet execute acquisition/leasing, registration/licensing (LTO), and onboarding to the fleet-management system (VS-06.2), sequencing with new-store openings (VS-37)

fields.Participants: Finance (VS-17.4), GL (VS-17.1), Store/DC Ops (VS-07/VS-04), Shared Services (VS-72/VS-103)
fields.Trigger: Annual budget (VS-33.1); operating model (W4244); monthly close (VS-17.1)
fields.Volume: Transport opex (fuel, vendor, maintenance, driver, allowance) allocated across 205 sites

workflows.name: Transport Budget, Cost Allocation & Chargeback to Sites

Automation Opportunity: - Rule-based cost allocation/chargeback posting; budget-vs-actual variance dashboards
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: budget approved (VS-33.1); allocation rule documented; intercompany arm's-length (VS-72); variance reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4/VS-33.1 (budget), VS-17.1 (GL/allocation), VS-72 (intercompany), VS-61 (fleet TCO), W4264 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Allocation-dispute risk**: Sites contest chargeback; mitigated by transparent, headcount/shift-based rule
- **Cost-leakage risk**: Unmonitored fuel/vendor inflation; mitigated by monthly variance review + analytics (W4264)
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks annual budget; monthly close allocation (part of VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Finance/Transport build the annual transport budget (fuel, vendor charter, owned-fleet opex, allowance, insurance) by site-cluster, aligned to the corporate budget (VS-33.1) and fleet TCO (VS-61)
Finance define the cost-allocation/chargeback rule (by headcount, by shift-served, or by site P&L) and post allocations monthly (inter-entity where BuildRight entities are served — coordinate VS-72)
Finance/Transport monitor budget-vs-actual, investigate variances with site managers, and feed cost analytics (W4264)

fields.Trigger: Operating model (W4244); regulatory change; annual review
fields.Volume: One transport governance/compliance framework + insurance program

workflows.name: Transport Governance, DOLE/LTFRB Compliance Framework & Insurance

Automation Opportunity: - Franchise/insurance/driver-license expiry registry with auto-alerts; digital pre-trip inspection checklist
Controls: - CTL-653: LTFRB franchise/LTO registration confirmed; passenger liability insured (VS-26); HSE transport standard documented (VS-24)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100.3 (legal), VS-22 (permits/compliance), VS-24 (HSE), VS-26 (insurance), VS-06 (fleet/driver), W4260 (compliance review)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Franchise risk**: Operating passenger service without LTFRB franchise → fines/impound; mitigated by franchise mapping & filings
- **Liability gap risk**: Under-insured passenger accident; mitigated by passenger-liability coverage (VS-26) and HSE standard
Time Estimate: - ~3 weeks annual framework; permit filings ongoing

steps.activity: Legal/Transport map the regulatory regime: LTFRB franchise for any operated/contracted common-carrier passenger service, LTO vehicle registration/inspection, DOLE OSH duty of care for employee transport, and driver licensing (professional license, PNP/LTO clearances)

Insurance/HSE structure the coverage (passenger- liability / vehicle insurance via VS-26, own-damage, acts-of-nature for typhoon-prone routes) and the HSE transport-safety standard (pre-trip inspection, speed, fatigue, no-phone)
Compliance document the framework, lodge any required permits/franchise filings (VS-22), train drivers/managers, and schedule periodic compliance review (W4260)

fields.Participants: EX (VS-103.2), People Analytics (VS-103.3), OpEx (VS-133), Labor Relations (VS-84)
fields.Trigger: Annual EX review (VS-103.2); attrition spike; feedback cycle
fields.Volume: Enterprise commute-EX program linked to attrition/attendance analytics

workflows.name: Commute Experience, EVP Linkage & Continuous-Improvement Plan

Automation Opportunity: - Commute-EX → attrition correlation analytics; route/comfort feedback → CI backlog (VS-133)
Controls: - CTL-653 (ensure controlled execution — Transport Strategy, Policy & Commute-Allowance Framework (PA-141.1).)
- CTL-653: commute-EX measured; attrition correlation tracked; CI loop closed (VS-133)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103.2/VS-103.3 (EX/analytics), VS-121 (employer brand), VS-102 (total rewards), VS-133 (OpEx/CI), VS-84 (labor), W4263/W4264 (route improvement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silent-attrition risk**: Commute pain unmeasured → preventable turnover; mitigated by commute-EX survey + attrition correlation
- **Disengagement risk**: Poor commute erodes EVP; mitigated by EVP linkage and CI loop
System Touchpoints: - EX/engagement (VS-103.2); people analytics (VS-103.3); employer brand (VS-121); OpEx (VS-133); comp (VS-102)
Time Estimate: - ~2 weeks annual EX cycle; CI continuous

steps.activity: EX/Analytics run the commute-experience survey and correlate commute difficulty with attrition, absenteeism, and engagement (VS-103.2/VS-103.3), prioritizing high-risk sites/shifts
EX link commute to the Employer Value Proposition / total-rewards narrative (VS-121 employer brand, VS-102 total rewards) and the attrition/attendance narrative with COO
EX/OpEx run a continuous-improvement loop on transport (route/timing/comfort changes per W4263/W4264), track EX uplift, and re-baseline
